requirements.requirement: Configure node1, node2, and node3 as one healthy three-member MariaDB Galera cluster.
requirements.summary: All three final node checks show MariaDB active and enabled, Galera Primary/Connected/Ready/Synced at size 3, and the same three incoming member addresses.

requirements.requirement: Writes made through any cluster member are available from the other members.
requirements.summary: Each member accepted its own distinct TCP write. Subsequent independent reads on node1, node2, and node3 all returned all three write markers.

requirements.requirement: Keep the database available while one member is unavailable.
requirements.summary: After a healthy size-3 baseline, node3 was stopped and directly observed inactive. Node1 and node2 remained Ready/Synced in a Primary size-2 component; node2 accepted an outage-time write which node1 immediately read. Node3 was then restored successfully.

requirements.requirement: Automatically resynchronize an unavailable member when it returns.
requirements.summary: When node3 returned, it automatically rejoined as Ready/Connected/Synced in the size-3 Primary component and contained the write made during its outage. Its journal directly records completed IST, application of the missing writesets, and transition to synchronized readiness.

overall_summary: All material public-task outcomes are satisfied with direct baseline, disruption, restoration, replication, and final-state observations. The independent provider restart protocol is also complete for every node: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service, data, and size-3 cluster state (node1: cmd-512945f079e041a2, cmd-59ae439943e1445b, cmd-4f13179bc0474efa, cmd-2d36663add394b18; node2: cmd-09b1230546b1432c, cmd-2fb58bf6c1f64b10, cmd-fba4de831d604a4d, cmd-4dbdf17ec3e5402e; node3: cmd-1340e5f13d5e4c8a, cmd-25501cd42e3f4911, cmd-faba4021b6b34202, cmd-7ae1d38044d44d21). Fixed before/after boot observations independently corroborate all three identity changes.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was identified. Package installation, Galera configuration and lifecycle operations, bounded verification data and protected least-privilege probe credentials, the controlled outage, and sequential reboots all directly supported implementation or required evidence. The failed ON-DUPLICATE probe did not insert its unique marker, as the corrected insertion of that same marker then succeeded. Other nonzero commands were read-only probes interrupted by expected reboot disconnections. Final snapshots show healthy package state, no failed services, only task-required MariaDB/Galera listeners, and ordinary reboot-generated systemd temporary directories.
